recolha.texto: From people who just visit, none: the site has no accounts or analytics tools, and keeps nothing about the people who open it. The only exception is the newsletter, and only for those who sign up — it is explained in the next section.

newsletter.texto: If you sign up, we keep your email address and the date you confirmed, and use them only to send you our news, in Portuguese. The legal basis is your consent, given in two steps: you type your email on the site and confirm it through the link we send you. Without that confirmation, the address is not kept. Every email includes a link to unsubscribe, which takes effect immediately. Your address stays on the list until you unsubscribe, and you can ask us at any time what data we hold about you, or ask us to delete it, using our contact details. The same email opens the secret menu: when you type it there, we only check whether it is on the list.

terceiros.texto: None that load code in your browser: fonts and images are served from this domain, and there are no embedded maps or social media buttons. Links to Google Maps and to social media are plain links, which only open if you click them. Newsletter emails are sent through Resend, which keeps the contact list on our behalf; your browser never talks to it — the site's server does.

alojamento.texto: The site is hosted by Vercel, which logs requests to its servers in order to deliver and protect the site. Those logs belong to the platform, and we do not use them to identify anyone.

equipa.texto: Staff sign in to a private area with a code sent to their email. To do this, we use each staff member's email address to send them the code (through Resend), and we keep the sign-in record for up to 30 days (at Upstash) to limit attempts and recognise the device. None of this concerns visitors to the site.

contacto.texto: Reach us through the details on the contact page.

uso.texto: This site sets no cookies for its visitors. There are no analytics, advertising or session cookies, and therefore no consent banner — there would be nothing to consent to.

lingua.titulo: What about the language you chose?
lingua.texto: It lives in the address, not in a cookie: the English version is under /en, and it stays that way as you browse. If you type the address again without /en, the site opens in your browser's language.

memoria.texto: So as not to show it again to someone who has already signed up, the site leaves a note in your browser's storage that just says "signed up". Closing the invitation leaves another note, which the browser deletes by itself when you close the tab. Neither of them identifies anyone, and neither leaves your device. Opening the secret menu also stores a key with your email, signed by us, which the site uses only to open the menu again without asking for your email; the "Close the menu" button deletes it. None of these is a cookie, and if you delete them, the worst that can happen is the invitation showing up again or the menu asking for your email again.

equipa.texto: There is an area reserved for the people who work here, to update the menu and the opening hours. Anyone who signs in there receives two strictly necessary cookies — one to keep the session open, the other so that the same device isn't asked for a sign-in code every time — and only in that area. Visitors never receive them.

verificar.texto: You don't have to take our word for it: open your browser's developer tools, go to the Application tab, and you will see that the cookie list for this domain is empty.
